clips.title: 中国不急推大刺激：出口复苏却与汇率脱钩，价值链上移能否持续？
title_lines: 出口复苏却与汇率脱钩
title_highlights: 出口复苏却与汇率脱钩

subtitles.en: Yeah, I mean, that's a pretty good question. I think when I think about the big picture in China, and even if I go as far back as the reopening trade, the market has clearly looked for some large headlines around fiscal stimulus.
subtitles.zh: 这是个好问题。思考中国大局，甚至回溯到重启交易，市场明显在寻找财政刺激的大标题。

subtitles.en: And we did get that in terms of direct equity markets stimulus in September 2024. And you know, to us in many ways, that was China's way of kind of experimenting with trying to see if positive wealth effects can be kicked in on a consumer from a consumer perspective by supporting equity markets very strongly and broadly.
subtitles.zh: 2024年9月我们确实看到了直接权益市场刺激。对我们来说，这在中国很多方面是一种实验，试图通过强力广泛支持权益市场，从消费者角度激发正向财富效应。

subtitles.en: But when I think about 2025, we moved on to essentially price that right tail out from Chinese equity markets on fiscal stimulus.
subtitles.zh: 但思考2025年，我们基本上已从中国权益市场中排除财政刺激的右尾风险。

subtitles.en: And I think for the right reasons, you know, when we look at the economy this year, it's been a very k-shaped path for China growth is below expectations, but pockets of the economy like exports are doing exceptionally strong driven by semiconductors.
subtitles.zh: 我认为有合理原因。看今年经济，中国增长呈非常K型路径，低于预期，但出口等领域受半导体驱动异常强劲。

subtitles.en: What's been interesting is that that export recovery is somewhat decoupling from the effect strength as well, which tells you that China is moving up in the value chain of exports as well.
subtitles.zh: 有趣的是，出口复苏在一定程度上与汇率强势脱钩，这说明中国在出口价值链上也在上移。

subtitles.en: So I think from a policy perspective, there is no rush here to come in to do big fiscal stimulus and equity market support is still extremely targeted to turn things around.
subtitles.zh: 所以从政策角度看，并不急于推出大规模财政刺激，权益市场支持仍非常有针对性以扭转局面。

clips.title: 巴克莱辛格：印尼市场评级下调，被动资金流出压力几何？
title_lines: 被动资金流出压力几何？

subtitles.en: Yeah, absolutely. Look, I think it's definitely been, you know, a surprise in terms of the announcement coming now, even though there was clearly a build up to it.
subtitles.zh: 当然。我认为现在宣布确实令人意外，尽管之前明显有铺垫。

subtitles.en: Indonesian assets are pretty cheap at these levels. Equities have obviously had some very large moves, MSCI Indonesia on a forward valuation basis is now as cheap as it's been since GFC.
subtitles.zh: 印尼资产在这些水平相当便宜。权益资产显然有大波动，MSCI印尼前瞻估值现在是全球流动性变化以来最便宜。

subtitles.en: And the Indonesian rupee in real terms is the cheapest that it's been in over 20 years.
subtitles.zh: 印尼盾实际汇率是20多年来最便宜。

subtitles.en: So clearly Indonesian assets are cheap, but I think there's a possibility that they get even cheaper in June, 20, 27 unless there are some very strong mitigating factors from a governance perspective.
subtitles.zh: 所以显然印尼资产便宜，但我认为2027年6月前可能更便宜，除非治理方面有非常强的缓解因素。

subtitles.en: We're expecting about 15 billion US dollars in passive equity outflows and we think dollar idea is likely to grind higher to 18 to 50 level by a second quarter of next year.
subtitles.zh: 我们预计约150亿美元被动权益资金流出，认为美元印尼盾可能在明年二季度前升至1850水平。

subtitles.en: And I think what that means for equities is, you know, unless again, there is a very strong turnaround in terms of what MSCI wants to see.
subtitles.zh: 我认为这对权益资产意味着，除非MSCI希望看到的情况出现非常强的转变。

subtitles.en: Equity rallies are probably going to be sold and you know, I'm heading into next year.
subtitles.zh: 权益资产反弹可能被卖出，进入明年。

subtitles.en: I think this is a very localized domestic story still when this announcement came out Indonesia's weight in EM indices was 50 bips.
subtitles.zh: 我认为这仍是非常局部的国内故事，公告发布时印尼在新兴市场指数中权重为50个基点。

subtitles.en: So by no means is this is this a broader even EM Asia contagion story, I would say as violent as the moves have been locally in Indonesia.
subtitles.zh: 所以这绝不是更广泛的新兴亚洲传染故事，尽管印尼本地波动剧烈。

clips.speaker: Marc Raibert
clips.title: 波士顿动力创始人：人形机器人竞赛，中国领先还是美国领先？
title_lines: 中国领先还是美国领先？

subtitles.en: Have you been impressed by the pace and could, you know, China continue to lead and extend its lead over the US perhaps when it comes to humanite robots.
subtitles.zh: 您对这样的发展速度印象深刻吗？中国是否可能在人形机器人领域继续领先并扩大对美国的优势？

subtitles.en: So, you know, I don't think in terms of a competition and I'm not sure I agree that China is leading or not leading. I do agree that it's a fantastic time to be in robotics. There's so much attention. There's so much resources, investors, and a lot's happening.
subtitles.zh: 我不从竞争的角度思考，也不确定是否同意中国领先或不领先。但我确实认为现在是机器人领域的绝佳时机，关注度极高，资源丰富，投资者众多，大量事情正在发生。

subtitles.en: You're right. Over the last couple of years, reinforcement learning is a technique that's really swept the globe. A number of different groups originated the work and now it's made it possible for a company to take their robot, apply those techniques.
subtitles.zh: 你说得对。过去几年，强化学习这项技术席卷全球。多个团队开创了这项工作，现在企业可以将这些技术应用到自己的机器人上。

subtitles.en: And almost immediately get it to do new, exciting things like you see at the Chinese Olympics or you see other companies using those techniques to do.
subtitles.zh: 几乎立刻就能让机器人做出令人兴奋的新动作，就像在中国奥运会上看到的那样，或其他公司运用这些技术所做的展示。

subtitles.en: You know, we see those robots lifting cars and doing backflips, but it's been hot for robots to actually do human action. I mean, David, my colleague was talking about we would love to see a robot mopping the floor, but it's not that easy to do what humans do as basic as they may seem.
subtitles.zh: 我们看到机器人举汽车、后空翻，但真正让机器人做人类动作一直很热门。我的同事大卫说，我们希望看到机器人拖地，但人类看似基本的动作并不容易做到。

subtitles.en: Absolutely true. I think part of the problem is that people don't understand how good human beings are at what they do.
subtitles.zh: 完全正确。我认为部分问题在于人们不了解人类在自己所做的事情上有多出色。

subtitles.en: And what versatility and dexterity and other features that humans have. I mean, I think at the root of it, there's a problem even in calling these robots humanoid.
subtitles.zh: 人类拥有多才多艺、灵巧以及其他特征。我认为根本问题在于，把这些机器人称为人形机器人本身就有问题。

subtitles.en: Because what does humanoid mean? Does it mean two arms, two legs and a head? Why are there maybe a hundred companies building robots with two arms, two legs and a head?
subtitles.zh: 因为人形意味着什么？是两条手臂、两条腿和一个头吗？为什么可能有上百家公司在制造有两条手臂、两条腿和一个头的机器人？

subtitles.en: When really humanoid should mean situational awareness, understanding our surroundings, mobility, dexterity, ability to use our hands or other parts of our body to move things around in a useful way.
subtitles.zh: 真正的人形应该意味着情境意识、理解周围环境、移动能力、灵巧性，以及用手或身体其他部位以有用方式移动物体的能力。

subtitles.en: Semantic understanding, understanding the world in a deeper way. All those ingredients are what make humans good at what they do and some animals good at what they do.
subtitles.zh: 语义理解，更深入地理解世界。所有这些要素让人类擅长所做之事，也让某些动物擅长它们所做之事。

clips.speaker_context: Founder of Boston Dynamics and Executive Director of the Robotics and AI Institute

clips.speaker: Marc Raibert
clips.title: 波士顿动力创始人：人形机器人五年后能做什么？仓库工厂先行，家庭尚远
title_lines: 仓库工厂先行，家庭尚远

subtitles.en: And I think if we focused on that, with a variety of morphologies involved, morphologies means two legs, two arms and a head or wheels and some other kind of body or maybe six arms, there's really no limit to what could be versatile and useful like a human.
subtitles.zh: 我认为如果我们专注于这一点，并涉及多种形态——形态意味着两条腿、两条手臂和一个头，或者轮子和另一种身体，或者六条手臂——那么像人类一样多才多艺和有用的可能性真的没有极限。

subtitles.en: So having said that, Mark, I'm wondering what's hype, what's not, five years down the road, what might these humanoid robots, whether you like the term or not, what would they be able to do?
subtitles.zh: 话虽如此，马克，我想知道哪些是炒作，哪些不是。五年后，这些你喜不喜欢这个称呼都罢的人形机器人，能做什么？

subtitles.en: It's hard to predict. I think that the easy thing to say is robots of various shapes and forms are already being used in warehouses and places like that, very organized things where there's objects being handled at very high volume.
subtitles.zh: 很难预测。容易说的是，各种形状和形式的机器人已经在仓库等场所使用，那些地方非常有序，物体处理量很大。

subtitles.en: And where it's hard to get human labor, human labor has a lot of turnover, there's aging populations, reduced populations, a lot of the attitudes towards some kinds of work is changing among young people, some populations are aging out for skilled labor.
subtitles.zh: 在难以获得人力劳动的地方，人力流动率高，人口老龄化，人口减少，年轻人对某些工作的态度在改变，一些群体的熟练劳动力正在老化退出。

subtitles.en: So there's a lot of pieces to the puzzle of what robots are going to be able to do.
subtitles.zh: 所以机器人能做什么这个谜题有很多拼图。

subtitles.en: Anyway, I start to say, I think warehouses are now factories are probably next, I think our homes are going to be a little ways out because for homes you need a lot of safety, you need really ultimate safety, you need low cost for consumers to be able to buy them and you need them to be able to do something useful in the home.
subtitles.zh: 总之，我开始说，我认为仓库之后，工厂可能是下一个，家庭则要远一些，因为家庭需要大量安全保障，需要极致安全，需要低成本让消费者买得起，还需要它们能在家里做有用的事。

subtitles.en: And given that everybody's house is different, everybody's junk is different, everybody's kids are there and vulnerable, it's a real challenge.
subtitles.zh: 考虑到每个人的房子不同，杂物不同，孩子在场且脆弱，这确实是真正的挑战。

clips.speaker_context: Founder of Boston Dynamics and Executive Director of the Robotics and AI Institute

clips.speaker: Marc Raibert
clips.title: 机器人威胁：被说透，创始人称多数是抽象概念
title_lines: 创始人称多数是抽象概念

subtitles.en: There's a lot of anxiety among people when it comes to being amongst robots and the potential of robots.
subtitles.zh: 人们对与机器人共处以及机器人的潜力有很多焦虑。

subtitles.en: You say that, but I take these robots around to shows when I give talks and people love to see here too.
subtitles.zh: 你这么说，但我演讲时带这些机器人去展会，人们也很喜欢看。

subtitles.en: Yeah, there's one right out there now and people love to see them, they love to pose with them.
subtitles.zh: 是的，现在外面就有一个，人们喜欢看它们，喜欢和它们合影。

subtitles.en: Until they become a threat or until they take over the jobs until, until we talk about possibly the extinction of humankind.
subtitles.zh: 直到它们成为威胁，或直到它们接管工作，直到我们谈论可能的人类灭绝。

subtitles.en: I think those are all abstract ideas that aren't as present as people think.
subtitles.zh: 我认为这些都是抽象概念，并不像人们想的那么迫在眉睫。

subtitles.en: I think the media likes to talk about those things more and certainly Hollywood thrives on those three things you just mentioned, I wish I could remember exactly what they were.
subtitles.zh: 我认为媒体更喜欢谈论这些，好莱坞当然靠你刚提到的三件事蓬勃发展，我希望我能记住具体是什么。

subtitles.en: You know, the threat, all those threats, I think the opportunities, look, we should take the risks seriously and work on providing safety in the robots, providing regulation and control.
subtitles.zh: 那些威胁，我认为机会……看，我们应该认真对待风险，努力提供机器人安全保障，提供监管和控制。

subtitles.en: But we shouldn't do it in a way that limits all the opportunities because the opportunities are vast and I'm hoping we get to take advantage of that.
subtitles.zh: 但我们不应以限制所有机会的方式来做，因为机会巨大，我希望我们能利用这些机会。

subtitles.en: There is a growing chorus of people who say, we need to slow down the development of AI, where do you sit on that debate?
subtitles.zh: 越来越多的人说我们需要放缓AI发展，你在这场辩论中持什么立场？

subtitles.en: I'm not sitting on that debate, I don't know, it seems overwrought to me, but you know, we'll see.
subtitles.zh: 我不参与那场辩论，我不知道，我觉得这有些过度紧张，但我们拭目以待。

subtitles.en: What's the worst case scenario?
subtitles.zh: 最坏的情况是什么？

subtitles.en: You know, I went to a meeting, an international meeting of government regulators and some of them would only talk about the worst possible thing that could happen.
subtitles.zh: 我参加过一个政府监管机构的国际会议，有些人只谈论可能发生的最坏情况。

subtitles.en: I don't think that's the right place to be, again, we need to talk about the balance of opportunity versus risks.
subtitles.zh: 我认为那不是正确的立场，我们需要谈论机会与风险的平衡。

subtitles.en: And if you just focus on the worst possible thing, I mean, we'd all be locked in our houses because a car might go by and we get hurt.
subtitles.zh: 如果只关注最坏情况，我们都会把自己锁在家里，因为可能有车经过而受伤。

title_lines: 最兴奋的是什么？生产力机会巨大

subtitles.en: So let's talk about the most positive thing.
subtitles.zh: 让我们谈谈最积极的事情。

subtitles.en: I mean, what are you most excited about when it comes to robotics?
subtitles.zh: 在机器人领域，你最兴奋的是什么？

subtitles.en: Where are we today?
subtitles.zh: 我们今天在哪里？

subtitles.en: Where are we headed?
subtitles.zh: 我们将走向何方？

subtitles.en: I mean, anything that is possibly the unimaginable that could happen?
subtitles.zh: 有没有可能发生难以想象的事情？

subtitles.en: I'll try and give two kinds of answers.
subtitles.zh: 我试着给出两种答案。

subtitles.en: So I'm a researcher developer and it's not all about making money for me, it's about making the technical advances and creating new things.
subtitles.zh: 我是研究员和开发者，对我来说不全是赚钱，而是取得技术进步和创造新事物。

subtitles.en: And you know, there's no necessarily end point in sight.
subtitles.zh: 而且不一定看得到终点。

subtitles.en: I mean, look at computers.
subtitles.zh: 看看计算机。

subtitles.en: You know, they made computers that were big and operated at one speed and then they got smaller and faster.
subtitles.zh: 他们造出又大又单一速度运行的计算机，然后它们变得更小更快。

subtitles.en: Now that you can carry them around, there's no limit to where the technology goes.
subtitles.zh: 现在你可以随身携带，技术发展没有极限。

subtitles.en: And robots are like that, too.
subtitles.zh: 机器人也是如此。

subtitles.en: So that's the researcher side of me.

subtitles.en: I do think that there's limitations to productivity for everybody.

subtitles.en: I think the, as I said before, there's aging population, there's declining populations, there's people who don't really want to work in the trades as much as they did.

subtitles.en: Now don't get me wrong, robots aren't up to doing what a plumber or electrician does yet, but they will be, I think.

subtitles.en: So there's an opportunity to have high productivity without necessarily having people available to do all those things.

clips.title: 美国情报：不再可靠，前军情六处首长说透

subtitles.en: It is a fragmented world and more and more countries are wanting more intelligence. Case in point, Japan.
subtitles.zh: 这是一个碎片化的世界，越来越多的国家想要更多情报。日本就是例子。

subtitles.en: It wants to form what is similar to the CIA. What do you make of that?
subtitles.zh: 它想组建类似CIA的机构。你怎么看？

subtitles.en: Well, I think two things are happening. First of all, the threat to countries like Japan and also to European countries like Germany has gone up.
subtitles.zh: 我认为有两件事在发生。首先，日本和德国等欧洲国家面临的威胁上升了。

subtitles.en: So you need better intelligence on the threats that you're facing and not just the capability of your opponents but what they're intending to do as the key bit of intelligence is intent.
subtitles.zh: 所以你需要更好的情报来应对威胁，不仅是对手的能力，还有他们的意图，因为情报的关键是意图。

subtitles.en: And at the same time, the Americans have become a less reliable partner in intelligence sharing and so you have to be more self-sufficient.
subtitles.zh: 同时，美国在情报共享上变得不那么可靠，所以你必须更加自给自足。

subtitles.en: So I'm not surprised and I welcome moves by Japan, by Germany and other countries which don't have a long tradition of providing more than effective skilled intelligence.
subtitles.zh: 所以我不意外，也欢迎日本、德国等没有长期提供高效情报传统的国家采取行动。

subtitles.en: So it is realistic. How long do you think it would take for Japan to get there?
subtitles.zh: 所以这是现实的。你认为日本需要多久才能达到？

subtitles.en: Well, it has taken us a hundred years to get MI6 to where it is. So these things do not happen overnight.
subtitles.zh: 我们花了100年才让军情六处达到今天的位置。所以这些事不是一夜之间发生的。

subtitles.en: You have to build up a culture, you have to build up an expertise within the organization.
subtitles.zh: 你必须在组织内建立一种文化，建立专业知识。

subtitles.en: You have to have the technology which enables you to run secret agents in a world of very great surveillance.
subtitles.zh: 你必须有技术，能在高度监控的世界里运行秘密特工。

subtitles.en: So I think the Japanese will need some help there reaching out to other partners like ourselves to provide that assistance.
subtitles.zh: 所以我认为日本在这方面需要一些帮助，向像我们这样的伙伴寻求协助。

subtitles.en: But you have to start somewhere and I think now is a good time for Japan, Germany and others to move out of the post-World War II mindset that you don't build up offensive intelligence services and you rely on your partners to provide you with the intelligence you need.
subtitles.zh: 但你必须从某处开始，我认为现在是日本、德国等国摆脱二战后思维的好时机——那种不建立进攻性情报机构、依赖伙伴提供所需情报的思维。

subtitles.en: We're moving on from that world now and one big component of it is the United States has become America first is not prioritizing the needs of its allies.
subtitles.zh: 我们正在离开那个世界，一个大的因素是美国的“美国优先”不再优先考虑盟友的需求。
